scope: All 597 kind=acc benchmarks in data/benchmarks.json, against data/results.json (11,691 results) at reviewed-data HEAD a9ba4e3 (whatmodel c7b3953). No data/*.json or existing file edited. Proposals follow the rule: only a baseline the source itself states, or the mean of per-setting baselines the source lists. The 2026-10-07 'set' decisions were not revisited. Entries marked 'Reopens 2026-10-07' were left at 0 then under the strict 1/k rule and are proposed now only because the source publishes a random baseline.
how_chance_is_applied: lib/score.ts toLatent: y = logit(clamp((score - c)/(1 - c), 0.005, 0.995)). Any score at or below c gets y = logit(0.005) = -5.29. A score just above c gets a very negative y too: with c = 0.277, a score 0.011 above chance gives y = -4.17.

effects.method: Refit in memory: lib/data.ts results + benchmarks with chance replaced; per category toCells -> connectedCells -> fit (as lib/data.ts comparisonSets). g on the 50 +/- 15 scale; delta = g_after - g_before for the same model. Threshold for listing: |delta| >= 1.

summary.headline: Only two proposals move any model by 1 point or more: bbh (7 models, at most -4.8, gemma-3-270m) and copen-cic-zero-shot-full-prompt (6 models, at most ±14, all with just 3 copen results). The seven vision/video proposals (mvbench, mmmu, mmmu-pro x3, mathvista-mini, math-vision, videommmu) each move no model by more than 0.1, because every result sits far above the baseline.
summary.near_chance_amplification: toLatent maps (score - c)/(1 - c) through a logit clamped at 0.005, so results a few points above the baseline become very low latents and results at or below it all share the floor (-5.29). Under copen-cic 0.277, gpt-neo-125m (0.288, 1.5% of the way above chance) lands at -4.17 while t5-small (0.401) lands at -1.76. g moves from 22.2 to 7.9 and from 22.5 to 36.2, from an 11-point raw gap. The already-applied open-pt 0.3264 does the same: phi-1 (0.2754), gemma-3-270m (0.2819) and tinyllama-1-1b-chat (0.2822) now share GPT-1's floor. tinyllama's only result is open-pt, so it went from 13.2 to -6.9, tied with GPT-1 (which went from -39.1 to -6.9). This is how the transform works, not a data error, but the choice of floor (0.005) decides how far below the field an at-chance model lands.
summary.bbh_note: The paper's 25.7 averages its 23 tasks. Sources that average the 27 sub-tasks would have a random level of about 25.2, within half a point.

failed_run_influence.what: Diagnostic only, not a deletion proposal: each suspected failed run's current share of its model's g (from fit.explain), the g that cell implies on its own, and the model's g if that one result were left out.

The biggest current pulls are granite-4-0-350m gpqa-diamond (share 0.37, -4.6 g), deepseek-r1-0528-qwen3-8b gpqa-diamond (-2.9) and llama-3-1-nemotron-ultra-253b bfcl-v4 (-2.7; bfcl-v4 has chance 0, so no floor applies). The zephyr OpenChat-card rows sit in a 3-model run and weigh under 1%.

floor_scan.rule: Every kind=acc benchmark, over all its results (any evaluator): lowest score, model, next-lowest and gap. Flags: 'gap>15' = lowest is more than 15 points below every other result; 'below-chance' = lowest is under the recorded chance. Most gap>15 rows are genuinely weak models on generative or agentic tests (chance 0 is correct there); the failed runs that were followed up are in failed_runs.
